- P50 and P95 targets for the hosted text-generation endpoint (we use short prompt workloads, median and tail matter).
- Measurement windows: are p50/p95 measured per-request, per-minute buckets, or a rolling window? We need reproducible definitions so our SREs and procurement can validate.
- Exception handling during our year-end surge window (Dec 15–Jan 10). Will that be excluded or covered?
- Credit model: what credits do you offer for missed commitments and any caps?

I've attached a short PDF that summarizes our expectations and a sample SLO language (atlas-slo-request.pdf). Procurement is looking for a response by EOD Monday so we can start legal review.

Hi Nora —

Appreciate the clear asks and the sample SLO language. High-level proposal below; attaching a draft amendment and a mutual action plan for timelines.

1) Target values (hosted text-generation default route):
   - P50: 120ms (median per-request server-side compute latency; excludes network egress)
   - P95: 420ms (95th percentile measured across customer requests hitting the same model variant)

2) Measurement methodology (proposed):
   - Per-request compute latency is recorded at the Redwood edge (time from request dequeue to final token returned).
   - P50: computed as the median across 60-second aggregation buckets, published hourly (we find this removes microsecond jitter while reflecting user experience).
   - P95: computed as a rolling 12-hour 95th percentile across the same per-request samples (this balances responsiveness to regressions and noise during short bursts).

3) Exception / surge handling:
   - We propose a negotiated exclusion window for AtlasHealth's known year-end surge (Dec 15–Jan 10) if you provide traffic forecasts 30 days in advance. During the exclusion window, we will provide best-effort support and capacity planning; standard credits will not be applied.

4) Credits and caps:
   - Credits for sustained breaches: tiered credit up to a 2% monthly recurring revenue cap for the first 90 days after go-live (pilot period).
   - Post-pilot, credit caps align to standard account terms (see draft amendment).

5) Rollout and validation plan:
   - 30-day canary with synthetic traffic + Atlas test tokens. 7-day joint validation window to confirm telemetry alignment.

I've attached the draft amendment (redwood-draft-amendment.docx) and a mutual-action-plan CSV with milestones. If this is acceptable, happy to have Marissa loop in legal and route this to DocuSign.

Two internal notes: we recommend approving the 12-hour rolling window (instead of 24) for Atlas given their expected traffic patterns — it's more responsive for a smaller-volume tenant. CC'ing Rishi to flag product implications.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Final terms (summary):

- P95: 420ms (95th percentile measured as a rolling 12-hour percentile across per-request samples).
- Measurement reporting: hourly published metrics with per-route breakdowns. We will provide a daily SLO report during the first 30 days of go-live for joint validation.

- Credits & caps: Breach credits up to 2% of monthly recurring charges during the first 90 days after go-live. After the pilot period, standard credit limits apply per the main SLA.

2) If acceptable, we've created a DocuSign envelope for the amendment here: https://docusign.com/envelope/exampleATL (please route to your legal).
